note: Written 21 Sep 2026. The corpus had been collected since August without a config, which is why the award sweep below had never been run. The method lives in .claude/skills/consensus-guide/SKILL.md.

awardBodies.name: National Breakfast & Brunch Awards
awardBodies.note: NOTHING TO CITE YET. Hosted by Quick Serve magazine (H2O Publishing). Sixteen finalists cook a signature round, a technical round, an omelette challenge and a brunch-at-speed round in front of industry judges. The first final is 23 February 2027 at Big Penny Social, London; entries close 6 November 2026. The domain is a frameset around the cognito entry form and publishes no results - the 2024, 2025 and 2026 form URLs all 404, only 2027 resolves - so the winners will have to be read from quickservemagazine.co.uk, the same way the National Burger Awards results are. RE-COLLECT AFTER 23 FEBRUARY 2027.

awardBodiesRuledOut: La Liste - checked laliste.com/news/laliste-hotels-2026-global-ranking-hospitality-trends-and-special-awards. Thirteen Special Award categories in the 2026 hotels edition and none of them is breakfast. Its Pastry Special Awards carry the afternoon tea title, not a breakfast one.
Harden's - hardens.com/london-restaurants/best/breakfast and /brunch both 404, and /awards renders as navigation to a fetcher (trap 15).

The World's 100 Best Coffee Shops - real, judged and dated, but its three London entries (Rosslyn, Moonstruck, Oma) are coffee shops already carried by the coffee corpus and none of them is a breakfast room. Recording it here would be trap 13.
National Restaurant Awards - judged and dated, but it ranks restaurants, not breakfasts. Printing its rank in a breakfast guide would be trap 7.

editorialLists.name: The Infatuation
editorialLists.note: Its brunch guide is grouped by compass point - Central, North, East, South, West - not ranked. Those headings extract as venue names; check them out before recording.

editorialLists.name: Time Out
editorialLists.note: Its greasy spoons list IS ranked, 1-8. Trap 11.

editorialLists.name: The Nudge
editorialLists.note: The widest list in the corpus at 51 names, but the page is client-rendered: curl returns the app shell and a map loader, so it has to be read in a browser.

editorialLists.name: The Good Food Guide
editorialLists.note: Tier A by domain, but its 'best breakfasts in central London' is an editorial feature, not a judged ranking - so hasAward on those twelve venues does not mean they hold an award.

editorialLists.name: Resy
editorialLists.note: Dated 2022 - the oldest list in the corpus.

editorialLists.name: James Dimitri
editorialLists.note: The specialist that carries the whole cheap end: 25 caffs with the price of each full English. 403s curl, so the prices already recorded in the corpus are the copy of record.

facetAxis.note: Breakfast splits by format rather than by cuisine, and the split is what the guide is organised on.

values.label: Australian brunch
values.describeAs: hotcakes, avocado and a serious flat white, the style London imported around 2010

values.label: The fry-up

values.label: Coffee-first

values.label: Weekend-only
values.describeAs: a kitchen that only cooks brunch on Saturday and Sunday

knownGaps: Community tier (E) is empty. Reddit is blocked in this environment.

Rise & Dine Cafe is named by two sources with two different prices - James Dimitri has the full English at GBP 11.99, @joshucr at GBP 5 - and neither publishes an area, so it is in the corpus and deliberately not on the page.
The Nudge is the largest single source here at 51 names and its page will not render to curl, so any re-collection from it has to be done in a browser.
openVenueQuestions: 'Sunday' in Barnsbury and 'Sunday in Brooklyn' in Notting Hill are two different restaurants, both in the corpus, and the shorter name is also an opening-hours row in other sources - it is carried by data/name-noise.json venueExceptions for this topic only.

'Burnt' and 'Burnt Bethnal Green' are both recorded from The Infatuation's brunch guide. The guide covers the Bethnal Green site as Burnt Arches; the two names have not been merged because the group also has Shepherd's Bush and a RADA cafe.
